newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South African President Nelson Mandela made a brief stopover in Dubai on Saturday on his way to Indonesia and met with the UAE's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Hamdan bin Zaid al-Nahayan.

- The ministry of health is urging baby food manufacturers to stop distributing samples at child care centres and hospitals in the UAE saying such promotions could impede the ministry's efforts to encourage breastfeeding, a ministry official said.
- Dubai on Saturday announced it was banning smoking at children's playgrounds in shopping centres and called for the allocation of smoking sections in restaurants and food courts.
- Share ownership in Abu Dhabi's $3 billion trade zone to be built on the Gulf island of Saadiyat will be open to local and foreign investors within two months, the project's hgeneral manager said.
- Water supply in some parts of the UAE emirate of Sharjah was cut off on Saturday due to an diesel spill on Friday, Sharjah municipality officials said.
- The value of Dubai's non-oil foreign trade reached around 82 billion dirhams in 1996, up 13.4 percent from 1995, the Dubai Economic Department said.
- The subscription of Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank attracted investments of 12.5 billion dirhams.
